## SLIDE 1 — Title
- Does cell-weighted sensitivity hide hard Patient-IDs?
- A pre-registered Patient-ID–stratified re-evaluation of a ResNet-50 malaria cell classifier
- NIH/NLM segmented thin-smear cells (27,558 crops) | base paper: Rajaraman et al. 2018 (PeerJ 6:e4568)
- CSA431 Computer Vision | M4 implementation + ablations · M5 failure analysis, IEEE paper, defence
- Team: [names]

## SLIDE 2 — Problem
- Papers on this dataset headline pooled, cell-weighted accuracy (often 96–99%)
- Cells are not independent: cells from one source share stain, light and focus
- Rajaraman already split by patient: 98.6% cell-level → 95.9% patient-level accuracy
- Open question from M1: under a leakage-free split, does a pooled mean hide source groups with concentrated false negatives?
- Rules we follow: predict before experimenting; report sensitivity + AUC; no clinical claims

## SLIDE 3 — Reproduction recap (M2)
| Metric | Published | Measured (M2) | Fold SD | Difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Accuracy | 95.9% | 93.90% | 1.95 pp | −2.00 pp |
| Sensitivity (recall) | 94.7% | 94.24% | 3.36 pp | −0.46 pp |
| Specificity | 97.2% | 93.56% | 1.30 pp | −3.64 pp |
| AUC | 0.991 | 0.9832 | 0.0086 | −0.0078 |

- Frozen ImageNet ResNet-50 features → 2048→512→1 FC, dropout 0.5; 5 folds grouped by the official NLM Patient-ID key (201 IDs; zero overlap)
- Close on sensitivity; lower on accuracy and specificity → an approximate reproduction (paper folds, layer and search not published in our source)
- Figures: `results/baseline/figures/baseline_roc_curve.png`, `baseline_confusion_matrix.png`

## SLIDE 4 — Hypothesis and prediction (recorded 3 Oct 2026, before any M4 code)
- **IF** the frozen M2 predictions are summarised per Patient-ID within each fold, **THEN** Patient-ID-macro sensitivity < pooled sensitivity, **BECAUSE** groups share appearance and contribute very unequal cell counts
- Predicted mean macro − pooled: about −1 to −3 pp
- Rule: SUPPORTED if ≥ 4/5 folds negative **and** mean ≤ −1.68 pp (half the M2 sensitivity fold SD, 3.36 pp); UNSUPPORTED = mirror; else INCONCLUSIVE
- Proof of timing: `milestones/m3/hypothesis.md` first committed in `f3152be` (03 Oct 2026 23:48 +0530), after the M2 metrics were written

## SLIDE 5 — Method: the one change
- Same model, features, probabilities, 0.5 threshold, labels, folds: **only the aggregation changes**
- Pooled = Σ TP / Σ (TP + FN) over the fold's cells; macro = mean of per-ID sensitivity over IDs with ≥ 1 Parasitized cell
- 151 IDs have Parasitized cells; 50 have none and are counted, not dropped
- Reuse assertions first: 27,558 rows, folds identical, no ID in two folds, pooled metrics recomputed to within 1.1e-16
- No significance test: with n = 5 pairs, the smallest two-sided exact Wilcoxon p is 0.0625; we report effect sizes + CIs

| 1 | 30 | 95.31 | 91.15 | −4.16 | [−7.58, −0.93] |

- Predicted: negative, −1 to −3 pp → Observed: 4/5 folds negative, mean −1.56 pp (inside the predicted range)
- Threshold −1.68 pp **not met** (short by 0.12 pp) → **INCONCLUSIVE**

## SLIDE 7 — Ablations (exploratory; the verdict does not change)
| Ablation (exploratory) | Setting | IDs | Mean Δ (pp) | Folds < 0 | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Primary (M3 rule) | macro, >= 1 Parasitized cell | 151 | −1.56 | 4/5 | verdict INCONCLUSIVE |
| A1 weighting | per-ID, weighted by cells | 151 |  | - | identical to pooled in all folds (max abs. difference 0.0e+00) |
| A2 eligibility | >= 10 Parasitized cells | 121 | −2.00 | 4/5 | 98.9% of positive cells kept |
| A2 eligibility | >= 25 Parasitized cells | 84 | −1.28 | 4/5 | 94.5% of positive cells kept |
| A3 leave-one-ID-out | 151 single-ID deletions | 150 remain |  | - | mean range −2.00 to −1.27; 2 change the verdict |
| A4 cluster bootstrap | 2,000 resamples, seed 42 | 151 | −1.56 | - | 95% CI [−2.95, −0.04] |
| A5 specificity | macro over IDs with Uninfected cells | 201 | +0.01 | 3/5 | 95% CI [−0.03, 0.05] |
| A5 accuracy | macro over all IDs | 201 | −0.03 | 3/5 | 95% CI [−0.57, 0.55] |

- A1: weighting each ID by its cell count gives back the pooled value exactly → the gap is purely the weighting
- A2/A3: an eligibility tweak or deleting one ID (C116P77ThinF (fold 2), C182P143NThinF (fold 5)) can flip the verdict → **fragile**; we keep the pre-registered verdict
- A5: specificity cannot move: every ID has 63–77 Uninfected cells, but 1–633 Parasitized

## SLIDE 8 — Failure analysis (1/2): where the errors are
- 795 false negatives; top Patient-ID (C116P77ThinF) holds 14.3%; top 10 hold 51.4%; 10 IDs hold half
- False positives are more diffuse: top 10 hold 29.7%; 28 IDs needed for half
- Fold 2 (the positive fold): 325 FN, 6 of the 10 worst IDs; its top ID holds 35.1% → large **hard** IDs pull pooled *below* macro
- Confident errors: 228 FN with p < 0.1 (28.7%), 217 FP with p > 0.9 (24.5%); Brier 0.0469, ECE 0.0116
- Figures: `results/m5/figures/error_concentration.png`, `reliability_diagram.png`

## SLIDE 9 — Failure analysis (2/2): what the worst cells look like
| Group (blind review) | Cells | IDs | Inclusion yes | No | Unclear | Grey/blue or atypical stain | Blur | Segmentation artefact | Possible label noise |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Top FN (lowest p) | 24 | 17 | 2 | 17 | 5 | 20 | 0 | 4 | 17 |
| Top FP (highest p) | 24 | 22 | 21 | 0 | 3 | 8 | 0 | 8 | 21 |
| Random TP | 24 | 19 | 24 | 0 | 0 | 9 | 1 | 8 | 0 |
| Random TN | 24 | 24 | 0 | 21 | 3 | 13 | 0 | 4 | 0 |

- Blind review of 96 crops by one **non-expert** reviewer (the AI assistant), categories fixed before viewing; official, hash-verified images only
- 17/24 most-confident FN show **no** visible inclusion; 21/24 most-confident FP **do**
- Observation, not cause: consistent with label noise (cf. Wilm et al. 2025), faint parasites, border debris, or reviewer error
- Figure: `results/m5/figures/grid_top_false_negatives.png`, `grid_top_false_positives.png`, `grid_worst_patient_ids.png`

## SLIDE 10 — Limitations
- n = 5 folds from one grouping seed → no significance; fold signs could change with a different grouping
- Verdict is near the threshold and fragile to single IDs; exploratory variants are not adopted
- Patient-ID is the official mapping key, not a slide or a diagnosis; one source patient has two keys
- Approximate reproduction (specificity −3.64 pp vs published); failure modes describe this model
- Image review: one non-expert reviewer, small crops, confidence-selected errors
- One public segmented-cell dataset; **no clinical claim**

## SLIDE 11 — What we would do next (each is a separate, new intervention)
- Repeat the grouped split with several seeds to see how often the sign flips
- Expert (microscopist) re-review of the confident errors, with inter-rater agreement
- Stain/acquisition-aware analysis of grey/blue-tinged crops
- Recalibration only as its own pre-registered change
- Always report pooled **and** per-Patient-ID sensitivity with the group distribution

## SLIDE 12 — Conclusion
- Reproduced Rajaraman's patient-level ResNet-50 baseline approximately: sensitivity 94.24%, AUC 0.9832
- Pre-registered one evaluation change; outcome **INCONCLUSIVE**: right direction in 4/5 folds and inside the predicted range, but short of the threshold
- Main lesson: whether cell weighting hides or exaggerates hard groups depends on which groups are large
- Errors concentrate in few Patient-IDs; the most confident errors may be label questions
- Public dataset research; no clinical claims
